<thought>Based on the mass (≈ 224 Da, corresponding to C₁₆H₁₆O) and the ¹³C NMR (13 aromatic carbons, a carbonyl at ~197 ppm, and three aliphatic carbons typical of a benzylic propyl chain), the structure that fits is a benzophenone bearing a propyl substituent on one phenyl ring. A concise SMILES for 4‑propyl‑benzophenone is:

CCCc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)c2ccccc2

This SMILES is valid, matches the molecular formula C₁₆H₁₆O, and is consistent with the observed spectra.</thought>
<final_answer>CCCc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)c2ccccc2</final_answer>
